2. Set price_usd: both periods fall under the same OpenEI tariff window (2025-01-01 to 2026-04-09), same $18.38 fixed monthly charge, and same tier-1 variable rate ($0.0263125 + $0.13441 = $0.1607225/kWh; both usages are below 2,000 kWh), so price_usd = 0.00.

3. Set days_usd: both periods are 30 days; the fixed charge is monthly and flat, not prorated, and there are no per-day variable charges, so days_usd = 0.00.

4. Estimate weather_usd: using the NOAA bill history, model kWh against CDD/HDD (optionally controlling for days), isolate the weather-attributable kWh difference between last month (CDD 368, HDD 0) and the current period (CDD 353, HDD 0), and value those kWh at the effective variable rate (~$0.1607/kWh).

5. Compute usage_usd as the residual so that price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals exactly +$13.65.

6. Screen for a billing error: reconstruct the expected tariff total for 1,281 kWh ($18.38 + 1,281 × $0.1607225 ≈ $224.27), compare it to the stated $231.00 and line items (riders match the adjustment rate; energy charge ≈ $40.44 vs expected ≈ $33.71), and verify billed kWh equals the meter difference. Since the gap (~$6.73) exceeds normal rounding, set billing_error_suspected = true and billing_error_usd ≈ 6.73; otherwise false/null. Return only the JSON object with the required keys.
